Are there any historical events that even in retrospect you're sure that couldn't have been predicted?

Wouldn't most historical events have been unpredictable? If predicting the future were all that easy, we'd be doing it now. I think the predictable event is the exception, not the rule. Even 3 months ago, for example, I'd never have guessed Donald Trump was going to actually be winning primaries in the spring.

I would say sometimes the general event is predictable but the specifics are not. For instance, a lot of people predicted that World War I was going to start at some point, but nobody knew for sure when it would start or that it was going to be an assassination of an Archduke in the Balkans that started it.

Natural phenomena (weather, earthquakes) have been unpredictable until recent times. Severe weather has been a factor in certain invasions (Mongol invasion of Japan, Napoleon invading Russia, The failure of the Spanish Armada) but I don't think the absence of the severe weather would have changed the overall outcomes of any of those scenarios.

At the risk of stepping into a minefield, I would say the rise of any specific religion over another could not have been predicted. Yes, humans have had temples and gods and mysticism for millennia, so predicting major religions to arise is not a big thing. But why does Christianity or Islam become so big and Zoroastrianism stay so niche? In Christianity's case, it went from niche to the official state religion of the Roman Empire with the Edict of Milan. I don't think that could have been predicted, but I will claim some level of ignorance.

EDIT: Okay, here is an event that would not have been predicted and that had a historical impact. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destruction_of_the_Library_of_Alexandria
